deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 80, c. 1981+): K is a combinatorial '1-dimensional' system of pseudo-lines. Each pseudo-line carries its cyclic sequence of crossing points (vertices), with arcs between consecutive vertices. The goal is to equip K with an 'orientation' (a coherent choice of local orientations, transports v_c along oriented arcs) and to show that when K comes from a genuine 2-dimensional arrangement X in the projective plane, this orientation is determined by the combinatorial data alone.

Previous page: take an arc a of the pseudo-line Θ joining privileged points s and s'. Choose pseudo-lines D through s and D' through s', both different from Θ, meeting at t. In the sub-system K' = K_{Θ,D,D'}, a triangle, let b join s to t on D. Let b' be the unique arc on D' from t to s' such that {a, b, b'} is compatible with the triangulation of K'. Then b and b' decompose into chains of arcs of K.

This page, formula (34): v_{a→} = v_{b'→} ∘ v_{b→}. Here b→ is b oriented from s to t and b'→ is b' oriented from t to s'. Both v's are defined as composites of the v_c over the K-arcs making up the paths (s,t) and (t,s'). In other words, transport along a is defined as transport around the other two sides of a triangle.

G. notes that, to get axiom (A3⁻), one must show this v_a is independent of the arbitrary choices (D, D', b). He has not checked this. He sets aside the degenerate cases where some pseudo-line of K is a 'digon' (only two privileged points). In particular this includes the near-pencil: n concurrent pseudo-lines cut by a single further one. These, he says, should be handled separately.

He then announces the next aim. For K coming from a 2-dimensional X, the (canonical) orientation should be describable purely from (K, (K_i)), the 1-dimensional system together with its sub-systems.

The next page carries this out for 3 concurrent pseudo-lines using an auxiliary 4th line Δ in general position. It relies on a Proposition: the functor (simple general 2-dimensional arrangements of 4 pseudo-lines) → (simple 1-dimensional arrangements of 4 pseudo-lines) is an equivalence of groupoids, proved by comparing both with the groupoid of arrangements of a 4-element set.

So the page serves the question of how much 1-dimensional (local-sequence-type) data determines the 2-dimensional pseudo-line arrangement and its orientation structure.
errors: No error, but an acknowledged gap: independence of v_a from the choices (D, D', b) is not verified, as G. says explicitly ('Je n'ai donc pas vérifié que la proposition ci-dessus soit correcte').
The degenerate cases (digon pseudo-line; n concurrent pseudo-lines plus one transversal, i.e. near-pencils) are explicitly left untreated.

ideas.what: Defining a transport/orientation datum on an arc by composing along the two other sides of a triangle formed with auxiliary pseudo-lines (formula (34)), with a required independence-of-choices axiom (A3⁻).
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle / flatness condition for a local system on the 1-skeleton of an arrangement; consistency of triangle orientations (chirotope-type axioms).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroid theory (Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence 1978); in the pseudo-line setting, Goodman–Pollack.

ideas.what: Program of recovering the 2-dimensional (orientation) structure of a pseudo-line arrangement from purely 1-dimensional combinatorial data (K, (K_i)).
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of pseudo-line arrangements from local sequences / allowable sequences; chirotope from combinatorial type.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Felsner–Weil (local sequences determine arrangements, c. 2000).

ideas.what: Separating out degenerate configurations (near-pencils, digon lines) as exceptional cases.
ideas.modern_name: Near-pencil arrangements as the exceptional case in Sylvester–Gallai-type and rigidity statements.

missed.claim: Well-definedness of the triangle-composition transport v_a, i.e. axiom (A3⁻), is left unverified. The near-pencil/digon cases are deferred.
missed.quote: Il faudrait, dans cette optique, pour (A3⁻) savoir que ce v_a ne dépend pas des choix arbitraires qui ont été faits
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only a minor curiosity. The analogous consistency statements are covered by oriented-matroid / chirotope theory.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's aim to describe the orientation of an arrangement from 1-dimensional data, via a groupoid equivalence for 4 pseudo-lines, anticipates later results that local sequences determine simple pseudo-line arrangements. He frames it categorically, as groupoids and functors of arrangements.
missed.quote: montrer que dans le cas d'un K… provenant d'un X, son orientation peut se décrire convenablement en termes de (K,(K_i)) seulement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The categorical/groupoid framing of arrangement moduli is not standard in that literature, but the underlying combinatorial results are known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page with a definitional step and an admitted gap. The mathematics (consistency of triangle orientations, reconstruction from 1-dimensional data) lies within known oriented-matroid / allowable-sequence theory. The only mild interest is Grothendieck's groupoid-theoretic framing.
transcription_corrections: '(K, (R_i))' at the end is very likely '(K, (K_i))', consistent with the next page.
'une orientation peut se décrire' is probably 'son orientation peut se décrire'.
The left margin note reads roughly 'mais il y a l'argument ... de la page précédente' — uncertain.
Arc notation is b→ (s to t) and b'→ (t to s'); the paths are (s,t)→ and (t,s')→ — consistent with the given transcription.
